set.body:
Phase: core. Track: engine.

Outcome
We know the core's supported envelope. It is wide enough for the pilot, and beyond it the service refuses clearly.

Acceptance
1. Run the frozen workload (docs/engineering-workload.md, quick and stress profiles) against the packaged service and compare every answer with its independent oracle: inventories, content hashes, query answers, export hashes and the access matrix. No budget in docs/workloads/engineering-v1.json has passed yet. Record each as met or missed.
2. Add a pilot-sized study: about 60 participants and two sessions, close to 9,000 entries, about 25 GiB, with single files up to 2 GiB. Measure server-side import and acceptance, search, the study read, single-file and whole-release download, and adding one session.
3. Repeat the same reads with growing numbers of unrelated datasets, releases and grants, to show whether cost follows the caller's scope or the whole installation.
4. State the pilot's budgets in one table and meet them: page reads under one second; download at 20 MB per second or better; import and acceptance times a curator will wait for. A miss is fixed here or in CORE4.
5. State the supported limits in the documentation: entries per release, JSON size, file size, upload size. The boundary datasets of 10,000 and 10,001 entries behave as the workload expects: the second is refused before any durable work.

Not in scope
Browser memory when hashing large uploads; large studies come in through IN4. The wider qualification harness (Q01.2 and H04.2, parked).

Start from
- scripts/generate-engineering-workload.py and docs/workloads/engineering-v1.json.
- scripts/check-query-scale.sh.
- docs/architecture-assessment-2026-11-18.md, finding 5.

Evidence
A results table under docs/evidence with commands, environment and raw numbers.
set.title: CORE3: Scale: the frozen workload and a pilot-sized study meet stated budgets (was OPS01)
